title: Shadow Evals on Customer Data
tagline: Decide with evidence whether a new agent version is better on this customer's real traffic: golden sets from logs, trajectory grading in shadow mode, a calibrated LLM judge, and business metrics with confidence intervals.
why: Public benchmarks do not tell you whether the new prompt or model is better for this customer. Their logs do. The FDE turns past conversations into a golden set, runs the new agent in shadow mode next to production (it sees real inputs; its actions are never executed), grades the full tool trajectory, checks that the LLM judge actually agrees with humans, and ships only when the business metric improves and no guardrail gets worse.
covers: Golden set from logs: PII scrub, near-duplicate removal (shingle Jaccard), outcome labels, good/bad balance per intent, stable hash split
Trajectory grading: required tools in order, forbidden tools, key arguments, step budget, required answer facts; regression / fix diff vs production; promotion gate
Judge calibration: Cohen's kappa threshold sweep, confusion matrix, precision / recall, length-bias and position-bias warnings
Business metrics: rate definitions as filters, Wilson 95% intervals, two-proportion z-test, guardrails that block a ship
gaps: No model calls: the shadow agent's trajectories and the judge's scores are inputs
Near-duplicate detection is lexical; semantic duplicates need embeddings
The z-test assumes independent samples; use a paired test when the same tickets are replayed

ops.label: Golden set from logs
ops.help: 36 past tickets: order numbers and emails are scrubbed, near-duplicates dropped, unclear outcomes (some edits) excluded, and each intent gets both good and bad examples.

ops.label: Calibrate the judge
ops.help: 40 items with human pass/fail and a 1-5 judge score. Finds the best threshold by kappa, then checks for length and position bias: this judge favors whichever answer is shown first.

ops.label: Business metric
ops.help: First-contact resolution on 600 production vs 600 shadow tickets, with two guardrails. Ship only if the primary metric improves significantly and no guardrail is worse.
